To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GH receptors are expressed in a variety of tissues, that GH receptors are functional and can be expressed in heterologous systems, and that GH stimulates protein synthesis in GH-receptor expressing cells.
the expression of GH receptors by transfection of a cDNA into a CHO cell line results in the appearance not only of specific binding of hGH but also of a functional GH receptor.
expression of GH receptors on CHO cells results in the appearance specific binding of GH to the cells and the acquisition of GH responsiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cell line that expresses a functional GH receptor and responds to GH by increasing the synthesis of specific proteins.
the development of a cell-based assay for the screening of potential GH receptor ligands.
the molecular mechanisms of growth hormone action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GH receptor cDNA has been successfully expressed and that it confers the capacity to bind GH and to respond to GH in transfected cells.
GH receptors have been successfully expressed in mammalian cells and have functional activity.
GH stimulates protein synthesis in CHO cells that have been transfected with the GH receptor gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GH receptors can be expressed in CHO cells and that these GH receptors bind GH in a specific manner.
we have shown that the GH receptor has been successfully expressed and that the receptor is biologically functional.
the GH receptor has been cloned and expressed in a heterologous system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GH receptor has the ability to bind to its hormone and to mediate a biological response.
GH receptor expression in CHO cells resulted in the ability of GH to stimulate protein synthesis.
GH receptor cDNA can be used as a tool for the study of GH action in cultured cells.
